title_ar: كفارة من واقع أهله في رمضان أهي خاصة برمضان أم أنها في قضائه وفي كل فرض؟
title_en: The Expiation for a Man Who Has Intercourse with His Wife in Ramadan: Is It Specific to Ramadan, or Does It Apply to Making It Up and to Every Obligatory Fast?
body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته مسألة كفارة من واقع أهله في رمضان أهي خاصة برمضان أم أنها في قضائه وفي كل فرض؟ وما دليل قصرها على شهر رمضان أو تعميمها لكل فرض جزاكم الله خيرا الجواب : هذه الكفارة خاصة برمضان فإن الأصل عدم الكفارة و جاء الحديث الصحيح بوجوبها على من واقع امرأته في نهار رمضان صيانة للشهر الذي عظم الله حرمته و أوجب صيام كل يوم منه أما القضاء و النذر ونحوهما من الواجبات فلم يعين الله لها شهرا و لا يوما
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. The question of the expiation (kaffārah) for a man who has intercourse with his wife in Ramadan: is it specific to Ramadan, or does it apply to making up the fast and to every obligatory fast? And what is the evidence for restricting it to the month of Ramadan, or for extending it to every obligatory fast? May God reward you well.

Answer: This expiation is specific to Ramadan. The baseline presumption is that there is no expiation, and the sound (ṣaḥīḥ) hadith came establishing that it is obligatory (wājib) upon a man who has intercourse with his wife during the daytime in Ramadan — as a safeguarding of the month whose sanctity God has magnified and every day of which He has made it obligatory to fast. As for making up the fast, the vowed fast and the like among the obligatory fasts, God has not designated for them a month or a day.
translator_notes: الأصل عدم الكفارة is rendered 'the baseline presumption is that there is no expiation'. This is the uṣūl move that carries the whole answer: expiation is an exception requiring a text, so it does not extend beyond the case the text names.

The questioner asked for the evidence on both sides. The Sheikh gives only the ground for restricting the expiation to Ramadan and does not set out a case for generalising it; nothing has been supplied for the side he did not argue.
